question: A finance team frequently asks Claude to build the same type of formatted spreadsheet report from raw data, and wants this repeated task folded into its existing reporting workflow without re-explaining the steps every time. Which capability best supports this?
options: A) Computer use lets Claude click through a spreadsheet application's interface for every report.
B) Agent Skills packages reusable spreadsheet-building instructions and scripts for reuse.
C) The citations feature makes every cell in the spreadsheet link back to a source sentence.
D) Prompt caching caches the raw data itself instead of storing the report-building instructions.
correct_answers: B) Agent Skills packages reusable spreadsheet-building instructions and scripts for reuse.
explanations: Incorrect. Computer Use could interact with a spreadsheet application, but it would require manually clicking through the interface each time, making it inefficient for a repeated task; it lacks the reusability of a packaged skill.
Correct. Agent Skills allow you to encapsulate reusable instructions and scripts, enabling the finance team to define the report-building process once and invoke it repeatedly without re-explaining.
Incorrect. Citations ground responses in source documents for verifiability, but they do not create links in spreadsheet cells; this feature is unrelated to packaging reusable report-building steps.
Incorrect. Prompt caching is meant to reuse prompt prefixes to reduce latency and cost, not to cache raw data; it does not provide a mechanism to store and reuse report-building instructions.
